/-!
# Erdős Problem 532

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/532](https://www.erdosproblems.com/532)
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial theory (1973), 117-138.
- [Er75b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Journées Arithmétiques de Bordeaux (1975), 295-310.
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory day (1977), 43-72.
- [Hi74] Hindman, Neil, *Finite sums from sequences within cells of a partition of $\mathbb{N}$*. J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. A (1974), 1-11.
-/

namespace Erdos532

/--
If $\mathbb{N}$ is 2-coloured then is there some infinite set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that
all finite subset sums$$ \sum_{n\in S}n$$(as $S$ ranges over all non-empty finite subsets of $A$)
are monochromatic?

Asked by Graham and Rothschild. Proved by Hindman [Hi74] (for any number of colours).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos532.lean"]
theorem erdos_532 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ (c : ℕ → Fin 2),
      ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧
        ∃ color : Fin 2,
          ∀ S : Finset ℕ, S.Nonempty → ↑S ⊆ A →
            c (∑ n ∈ S, n) = color := by
  sorry

end Erdos532

reformulations.difference: The original surveys describe a strictly increasing infinite sequence and its finite sums with coefficients in {0,1}; Lean uses an infinite set of natural numbers and sums over nonempty finite subsets. Lean's natural numbers also include zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each colouring, removing zero from an infinite witness preserves infinitude and monochromatic finite sums. Choose a strictly increasing sequence from the remaining set. Its finite index sets map injectively to finite subsets of the witness, preserving sums. Conversely, the range of a strictly increasing sequence is infinite, and every nonempty finite subset of that range has a finite preimage with the same sum. Nonzero finitely supported {0,1}-coefficients correspond exactly to nonempty finite index sets. The set-to-positive-sequence equivalence and zero-removal equivalence were proved independently of the admitted theorem in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states problem 532. Quantifier scope, the common colour, distinct summands, exclusion of empty subsets, and answer(True) are correct. Boundary checks covered empty and singleton sets, zero, constant colourings, and finite subset-sum computations. The source currently records an affirmative solution and a verified Lean proof, matching the metadata. The linked Lean 4.29.1 proof has exactly the required conclusion; after explicit Stream'.head/get unfolding at two steps for this checkout's newer Mathlib, it kernel-checks with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Hindman's original full text was inaccessible, but faithfulness was settled using the problem page and all three cited Erdős surveys. The reviewed file remains identical to the committed version.
